source_text: Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi: ideo et quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei. Si autem Filius Dei, etiam Deus, eiusdem formae cum Patre, et coaeternus: in quo omnem Pater possidet clarificationem: character atque imago in persona; et per splendorem gloria refulget. Et quemadmodum ex perenni fonte procedunt flumina: sic et ex hoc perenni ac semper vivo fonte, progreditur perennis et vera lux mundi, Christus Deus noster. De eo namque Prophetae clamarunt: Fluminis impetus laetificat civitatem Dei: neque unam duntaxat civitatem, sed omnes; nam sicut unam civitatem, universum terrarum laetificat orbem.
thought_title: The Holy Spirit and the Son of God
orientation: Gabriel is still speaking to Mary, explaining who the child to be born will be.
pass_a_gloss: The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you: for this reason also the holy thing that will be born from you will be called Son of God. But if Son of God, also God, of the same form with the Father, and coeternal: in whom the Father possesses all brightness: imprint and image in person; and through splendor glory shines forth. And just as rivers come forth from an everlasting spring: so also from this everlasting and always living spring comes forth the everlasting and true light of the world, Christ our God. For concerning him the Prophets cried out: The rush of the river gladdens the city of God: and not one city only, but all; for as one city, it gladdens the whole circle of lands.

pass_b_english: Gabriel went on: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy child to be born from you will be called Son of God" (Luke 1:35). If he is Son of God, he is also God, of the same form as the Father and coeternal with him. In him the Father holds all brightness. He is the imprint and image in person, and glory shines forth through his radiance.

Just as rivers come forth from an everlasting spring, so from this everlasting and ever-living spring comes forth the everlasting and true light of the world, Christ our God. For about him the Prophets cried out, 'The rush of the river gladdens the city of God' (Psalms 46:4). It gladdens not one city alone, but all cities. For as it gladdens one city, it gladdens the whole world.
